headlines.title: Apple, Alphabet and Uber survived major founder transitions. Nvidia will be a harder test
headlines.summary: Like Apple, Nvidia now faces its own transition away from a founder-led company. But experts say Jensen Huang’s central role could make replacing him difficult.
headlines.article_text: Nvidia after Jensen Huang: What founder transitions show Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Jensen Huang’s sudden resignation leaves Nvidia facing an unusually difficult transition after losing its founder CEO. Companies like Apple, Alphabet and Uber have prospered after losing high-profile leaders, but those transitions were generally less abrupt. Nvidia’s next permanent CEO will need to manage the fallout from Huang’s departure while maintaining its competitive position as rivals develop their own chips. In this article NVDA AAPL GOOGL UBER AMD SKHY Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., during a Bloomberg Television interview in London, UK, on Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. Jose Sarmento Matos | Bloomberg | Getty Images Jensen Huang is not the first CEO to leave a company he helped build. But experts told CNBC that his sudden resignation f rom Nvidia at a critical juncture is unique and leaves his eventual successor with challenges in leading the company that's powering the artificial intelligence boom. In 33 years, Huang, who resigned on Thursday amid reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman U.S. intelligence believes is a spy for China , made the company he co-founded the world's most valuable. Former Goldman Sachs CEO Lloyd Blankfein wrote on X that he was "indispensable" but "the graveyards are filled with indispensable men," referencing a quote attributed to French leader Charles de Gaulle. While the board looks for a new CEO and CFO Colette Kress does the job temporarily; analysts say Huang's charisma and bullish drive will be hard to replicate. "I'm not sure we've seen a situation quite like this, where the founder and CEO of one of the world's largest companies faces such a sudden departure amid scandal," Michael Withers, professor of management at the University of Notre Dame's Mendoza College of Business, told CNBC. Whoever follows will "face challenges that go well beyond those of a typical CEO replacing a founder," he added. watch now VIDEO 4:24 04:24 ASUS Co-CEO: to watch if Nvidia's new leadership can sustain AI industry growth Squawk Box Asia When founders step back Apple 's image was inseparable from Steve Jobs when he resigned in 2011. But unlike Nvidia, the company had had other CEOs — and an internal successor. Tim Cook invested in Apple's chip strategy and services business and became a key corporate diplomat in dealings with the U.S. and Chinese governments. He was known as an operator who controlled Apple's supply chain. Cook had "considerable preparation" for becoming CEO, Withers said. Apple's market cap went from about $350 billion to $4 trillion in his 15-year tenure. Larry Page and Sergey Brin left their executive roles at Alphabet in 2019, 21 years after founding Google. Page and Brin's departures were expected. Page said at the time that it was the "natural time" to simplify the company's management structure. Alphabet shares are up more than 300% since then under Sunder Pichai. Travis Kalanick left Uber in 2017 after mounting pressure over a series of scandals and governance concerns. But his departure "unfolded over several months, and while it certainly attracted attention, it pales in comparison to what Nvidia is currently facing," Withers added. Former Expedia CEO Dara Khosrowshahi repaired the organization and found a path to profitability . What's different about Huang's departure Withers said successor CEOs often struggle "under normal circumstances" to juggle maintaining what made a company successful while establishing their own leadership. "It becomes considerably more difficult when the transition follows such a high-profile scandal involving the company's founder," he added. Huang had an extraordinary 60 direct reports, as part of a flat structure that favored fast communication over layered hierarchies. Withers told CNBC Nvidia did not appear to have a succession plan for Huang, who is also often described as inextricably linked to the company. "We're talking about a company that was, until recently, the largest in the world by market capitalization. That's a pretty remarkable situation," he added. Challenges after Huang As well as having to "step out of his shadow," the new CEO will have to deal with the "scandal" arising from Huang's conduct and "the extent to which it sticks with Nvidia," Withers said. Huang's successor will also have to tackle the longer-term business strategy, while picking up the relationships he managed. Huang cultivated a close relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump and accompanied him to China in May . Huang consistently pushed for the U.S. to relax export restrictions that prevent Nvidia from selling its chips to the world's second-largest economy. He also managed close relationships with the bosses of the company's key suppliers, from SK Hynix to Samsung. Storm Uru, co-head of the Global Innovation team at Nvidia investor Liontrust Asset Management, said two key priorities were changing company culture and managing the supply chain. The supply chain was "where Jensen was able to provide a vision for the future and able to bring people to the table and to expand capacity to enable the build-out of this technology," Uru told CNBC, adding it mattered especially "when supply chains are already so tight." watch now VIDEO 2:19 02:19 Nvidia had no succession plan, this is 'a dark day for Nvidia,' says Yorkville Ives' Dan Ives Closing Bell Nvidia continues to face rising competition from rivals such as AMD and hyperscalers, which are ramping up efforts to develop their own chips. Investors noted that the new CEO will have a roadmap of products for the next few years, unaffected by Huang's removal. "We have to look beyond Jensen ... there are thousands upon thousands of engineers," Joanne Feeney, partner and portfolio manager, Advisors Capital Management, told CNBC on Thursday, as pressure was mounting on Huang to go. headlines.article_text: Microsoft outage continues, Outlook and other 365 services down Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points A Microsoft outage on Thursday and Friday affected users of services like Outlook, Teams and 365. The company said it did not suspect malicious activity was the cause and it was attempting to restore operations. Amazon Web Services said it was "operating normally" and noted inaccurate reports of outages on its platforms. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 2:27 02:27 Microsoft outage hits hundreds of millions, CNBC anchors can't read your emails Squawk Box Europe Microsoft suffered a widespread outage on Thursday and Friday, causing disruption to millions of its customers as engineers scrambled to fix one of its biggest-ever server issues. Connectivity issues began shortly before 1 p.m. ET on Thursday and continued into Friday, with Outlook and Teams, along with multiple Microsoft 365 services such as Sharepoint and Copilot, affected. Numerous external services that connect with Microsoft products such as Outlook Calendar were also hit. 'Encouraging recovery progress' A sign on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, Washington, US, Oct. 26, 2026. David Ryder | Reuters In an update shortly after 7 a.m. ET, Microsoft continued to warn that users may be unable to connect to multiple Microsoft 365 products, including Outlook on either web or desktop and many services that interact with email. However, it said it was making "encouraging recovery progress in Europe," with service availability and email delivery improving for some users. It said service is being "gradually restored" in the Asia Pacific and that the situation in North America was "improving." Intermittent issues are expected as recovery efforts continue. Email and related tools were unavailable for Microsoft users on Thursday afternoon and evening, throughout the Asian business day on Friday and across the European and early U.S. morning. Engineering teams have been taking affected systems offline for fixes and bringing them back online in stages. They are prioritizing efforts to preserve emails delayed during the recovery process and reduce email queues and backlogs, extending the timeout window, whereby delayed emails continue to attempt delivery, to 48 hours to help protect messages. Microsoft says it has not detected any malicious activity causing the outage, which it initially blamed on a traffic surge in part of its infrastructure and issues with a component responsible for processing server health. The company said in its initial updates on Thursday that the connectivity problems related to infrastructure "elevated load across multiple regions," caused by a "number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure." Some servers were failing automated health checks, it said. Microsoft shares were around 2% lower in premarket trade. Governments and businesses review impact Governments and businesses in Asia-Pacific and Europe said they were monitoring the situation, which was causing widespread disruption. The U.K.'s National Health Service said the outage was affecting some of its services but that patients should attend appointments as normal. Calls "may be subject to long waits" as a result of disruption to the organization, a hospital group serving South West London and the English county of Surrey said on X. Earnings for Swiss luxury goods giant Richemont were slightly delayed on Friday due to the outage. Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on Nov. 12, rescheduled the release to Nov. 16, citing business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outage. Air India said it had "temporarily rerouted" emails so it could continue to receive customer messages, adding that its flight operations were not affected. Australian Home Affairs and Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said in a press conference that Microsoft "believe they are dealing in some ways similar to what we saw with respect to CrowdStrike where there is an update that has gone awry," Reuters reported. A fault with an update issued by cybersecurity company CrowdStrike caused one of the world's biggest IT system outages in 2024 , hitting airlines, banks and more, Microsoft reported in 2025 that Copilot, its collection of AI assistants and tools, had more than 100 million monthly active users. Amazon Web Services and Google users also reported outages on the site on Thursday. Amazon wrote on X that services were "operating normally" and an "unrelated disruption elsewhere on the internet is prompting some inaccurate news reports." The company referred users to its health dashboard for "accurate data." At 4 p.m. ET Thursday, Microsoft said it had "validated an alternative service health check method" that brought some affected servers back online. "We're now applying this change more broadly," Microsoft wrote. "We're also preparing automated recovery systems to continually detect and restart unresponsive servers, to maintain service stability while this change progresses." headlines.title: Blossom Gold Receives Approval for Notices of Intent on the RBX Claims and Rosebud West to Advance Site Investigations for Planned Facilities and Water Supply
headlines.summary: TORONTO, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blossom Gold Inc. (“Blossom” or the “Company”) (TSX: BGAU, OTCQX: BGAUF) is pleased to announce that the U.S. Bureau of Land Management (“BLM”) has approved Notices of Intent (“NOI”) to conduct site investigation activities on the Company’s RBX claims and the Rosebud West area. The RBX claims, located southeast of the Rosebud claim block, are planned to host the Project’s primary infrastructure, including the ore conveyor, secondary and tertiary crushing, agglomeration and processing facilities, and heap leach pad as well as the planned waste rock storage facility. The NOI for Rosebud West is southwest of the Rosebud Claims and encompasses the water well field area where water is expected to be sourced for the Project.
